body:
For every `q ≥ 9`, the single-seed center column of rule 30 is not eventually the repeating word `1 0^q`, whatever the transient (`Rule30WhiteEndNine.not_eventually_white_end_ge9`). This revision follows the review of the previous version: the new module does not import `Rule30WhiteEnd`, it has no certificate data module, and `Rule30PaddedWords` lowers the bound for the tail `1` from `10` to `9`.

**One certificate, pumped over the white run.** The mode certificate `not_eventually_word_mode` (sound for every word, width, warm-up and label phase) is instantiated by one formula in `q`: `modeCert (1 0^q) 12 5 2 (reach 12 5 q) (reach 12 5 q ∧ lab0) (reach 12 5 q ∧ lab1)`, i.e. twelve cells, five warm-up periods, label phase `2`, the reachable set, and two fixed label masks. `lab0` is a closed form: column `1` two steps after the black cell is white exactly when the strip starts with `1` and has a `1` among its next two cells. `modeCert_white_end` proves this formula true for every `q ≥ 9`.

The pumping is as in `Rule30WhitePadding`. A period of `1 0^q` is one black step followed by `q` white steps. A chain of five sets, each the `10`-step white image of the previous one closed under white steps, is built and checked once (`pumpCheck_12 : pumpCheck 12 10 5 = true`, no `q` in it). Strip images are monotone, so for every `q ≥ 10` the reachable sets lie inside the chain, and each condition of the mode certificate follows from that one check (`modeCert_pumped`).

**Why `q = 9` is the base case of the same formula.** For `q ≥ 10` the label is `0` on every reachable strip. At `q = 9` the label `1` occurs on 21 reachable strips, so the labels may alternate. The same pumped check started at nine white steps fails, because its sets contain strips with label `1` (`pumpCheck_12_nine : pumpCheck 12 9 5 = false`, proved in Lean). This rules out that particular check, not every possible pumping. So `modeCert_white_end` has one statement and one formula, and the kernel evaluates that formula at `q = 9` (`modeCert_nine`) rather than pumping into it. We also looked for mode-certificate data independent of `q` that would cover `q = 9` as well, with sets closed under every period `1 0^q` with `q ≥ 9`. Such data would also certify the mixed words `1 0^q1 1 0^q2 …`. For every strip width up to `22` these mixed words have explicit codebooks: gaps in `[9, 16]`, replayed cell by cell in the strip relaxation, where two runs with the same center return to the same strip and differ in the label. There is therefore no such data at those widths; we claim nothing for wider strips.

**Bit-parallel images.** `fimage` computes the image of a set of strips with `O(K)` operations on `2^(K+1)`-bit numbers and is proved sound (`fimage_mem`). The module builds in about 3 s with 0.6 GB peak (16-core x86-64). `lake env lean --run Check.lean Ruliology.CellularAutomata.Rule30WhiteEndNine --claim partial --headline Ruliology.CellularAutomata.Rule30WhiteEndNine.not_eventually_white_end_ge9` returns `verdict: pass` with the standard axioms only.

**`Rule30PaddedWords`.** `paddedBound [true]` is `9`, `not_eventuallyWord_zeros_one` holds for `q ≥ 9` by rotating `not_eventually_white_end_ge9`, and the module imports `Rule30WhiteEndNine` instead of `Rule30WhiteEnd`. The other bounds are unchanged. The README rows and the catalog count (125 modules) are updated.

Research and formalization by Claude (Anthropic) for @AIOvernight.

AI used: Claude (Anthropic), with OpenAI Codex for independent review. Author: @AIOvernight.
